land.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia, Frankish since 785 and 794 and organised as the Carolingian Duchy of Saxony (804-1296) after 'the emperor Charlemagne conquered the Saxons' in 804

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the Franks over Saxony 788-792 and again from 800.

land.text: the part of the Saxons' former land in Holstein north of the Elbe, 'awarded to the Obotrites in 804, as a reward for their victory' (the Obotrites page adds 'This however was soon reverted through an invasion of the Danes')

successors.note: The Nordalbingia page has the Nordalbingian Saxons pardoned and their land restored after Charlemagne's death in 814.

keyframe_review.note: 6,335 km2 at the mouth of the Elbe (8.4-9.5 E, 53.3-54.5 N). The page: 'the original Saxon tribe lived north of the mouth of the Elbe'; Ptolemy's 'Saxones' 'just to the north of the lower Elbe'. The Chauci page has the Chauci, between the Ems and the Elbe, 'lost their separate identity in the third century when they merged with the Saxons' (an 'unsettled issue'), so the third-century Saxon ground may be wider than this core. No infobox area.

82,798 km2: Cliopatria's jump from the Elbe-mouth core (6,335 km2) to all of Old Saxony, 'the entire territory between the lower Elbe and Saale rivers almost to the Rhine'. No opened page dates it: the Old Saxony page says only that 'As land became scarce, the Saxon population began to expand southward'; Chlothar's 555 campaign in 'the upper valley of the Weser, Elbe, and the coast of the North Sea' and Charles Martel's 718 march 'to the banks of the Weser, the Lippe, and the Ruhr' attest the reach by then. Unverified: page budget. Area sanity: the page gives no area (Adam of Bremen's eight days' journey between the angles of a triangle).
82,596 km2; four cells (1,012 km2) fewer than 455-468 along the south-western edge: boundary noise, no event on any page. Unverified: page budget.

81,650 km2; a strip of 506 km2 added in the east (11.0-11.5 E) and 759 km2 lost near 11.4-11.8 E: boundary noise (the Lombards are Cliopatria's neighbour 490-499). No event on any page. Unverified: page budget.
82,596 km2: the 469 shape again. Unverified: page budget.

82,666 km2; one cell added at 9.5 E 51.3 N. The page: Theuderic and Chlothar 'conquered Thuringia' in 531; the Saxons page calls the later claim that Saxons helped 'unsupported by contemporary sources', so the Saxons gain no Thuringian land and the shape stands.

82,596 km2. Chlothar's 555-556 wars with the Saxons ended with a peace and a tribute ('an annual tribute of 500 cows'); the Saxons stay a separate, tributary state, so the shape stands (the Franks' dossier should carry the tribute as a vassal tint if it uses one).
82,317 km2; two cells (506 km2) lost at 7.1 E 53.0 N on the Ems, where Cliopatria's Magna Frisia begins (602): boundary noise or the Frisian border. Unverified: page budget.
82,386 km2: the 534 cell again; no event. Unverified: page budget.
82,338 km2: same area within a cell; no event. Unverified: page budget.
82,317 km2: same as 602. Unverified: page budget.

82,386 km2: the Saxons within Old Saxony across the age of Charles Martel. 718: he 'laid waste their country to the banks of the Weser, the Lippe, and the Ruhr'; 731 'after defeating the Saxons'; 738 'compelled the Saxons of Westphalia to submit and pay tribute'. None of this changes the frontier on the pages; Pepin took 'a tribute of 330 horses per year' in 758 (Saxons page). The shape stands as a tributary state's land.

correction.text: unchanged shape of 771: all Old Saxony, contested by the Franks from 772 (the Cliopatria patch is a campaign, not a conquest)

keyframe_review.note: 77,375 km2: Cliopatria gives a Westphalian patch (5,564 km2, 7.5-8.7 E, 51.2-52.0 N) to the Franks for 772-774. The page: in 772 Charlemagne 'subjugated the Engrians, and destroyed the Irminsul' at Eresburg, 'reached the Weser' and took hostages, then turned to the Lombards in 773-774 (no lasting control stated). So the whole of Old Saxony stays Saxon, contested from 772.

9,580 km2 around the Elbe mouth (8.5-11.2 E, 53.3-54.5 N): Nordalbingia. The page, 775: Charlemagne took Sigiburg, beat the Engrians and Eastphalians and left camps at Sigiburg and Eresburg; 'all Saxony except Nordalbingia was under his control'. Eresburg was lost in the 776 rising and retaken; the Paderborn diet of 777 treated Saxony as annexed. Cliopatria's Franks hold the rest 775-777.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 778 only: the Saxon rising of the year of Roncesvalles, to the Rhine at Deutz

keyframe_review.note: 82,364 km2: all Old Saxony independent 778-782. True only for 778, when Charlemagne was in Spain and 'the Westphalians again invaded the Frankish Rhineland' (Widukind page; 'the Saxons advanced to Deutz on the Rhine' on the Saxons page). In summer 779 he 'conquered Eastphalia, Engria, and Westphalia' and organised them into missionary districts and countships (Saxon Wars page); 780-781 are peace.

correction.text: Nordalbingia, the only Saxon ground left after 779

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the 779 conquest of Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia the Saxons hold only Nordalbingia, which the page leaves out of the conquered provinces ('he conquered Eastphalia, Engria, and Westphalia'); Widukind fled 'across the Elbe to Nordalbingia' (Nordalbingia page, 777). Peace 780-781: 'The land had peace from 780 to 782.'

correction.text: all Old Saxony, in revolt under Widukind

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'By 782, Widukind had returned from Denmark' (Widukind page); 'In the fall, Widukind led a revolt' and 'won the Battle of Süntel while Charles was campaigning against the Sorbs'; the Verden massacre followed. The rising restores all Old Saxony as a war zone.

82,386 km2 for 783-787. The page: 'From 782 to 784, battles between Saxons and Franks occurred annually'; Charlemagne wintered at Minden; in 785 Widukind surrendered in the Bardengau and was baptised, after which 'Charlemagne could have claimed to have conquered Saxony' and peace held about seven years. So the shape is right for 783-784 and 785-792 are Frankish (Cliopatria's own Franks hold Saxony 788-792 and has no Saxon shape then). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 783..784 from this entry's own 'valid for 783-784 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 793-794 only: the revolt of the Westphalians, Eastphalians and Nordalbingians

keyframe_review.note: 81,375 km2 for 793-799. The page: the Westphalians rose in 792 against recruitment for the Avar wars; in 793 'Eastphalians and Nordalbingians joined the revolt' and it was 'completely put down by 794'; an Engrian rebellion in 796 was crushed 'quickly'. So the full shape holds for 793-794; from 795 only Nordalbingia, where Bornhöved (798) and the 804 deportations were fought. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 793..794 from this entry's own 'valid for 793-794 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Nordalbingia, held until the Obotrites' 804 award

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 795-804 (Cliopatria's Franks hold all Saxony from 800). Nordalbingia is the last Saxon ground: 798 'Bornhöved, Frankish forces and their Obotrite allies ... defeated the Nordalbingian tribes' (Nordalbingia page); 804 'the last Engrian/Nordalbingian insurrection was effectively ended', the Nordalbingians deported and their lands given to the Obotrites (Saxon Wars and Obotrites pages). Soft: neither page says who held the rest of the Elbe-north country 795-797.

region.text: the mouth of the Elbe

ledger.note: 283: the Saxons live at the mouth of the Elbe. 'Some copies of this text [Ptolemy] mention a tribe called Saxones in the area just to the north of the lower Elbe'; 'the original Saxon tribe lived north of the mouth of the Elbe'; Eutropius's Saxon raiders near Boulogne 'in about 285' (called anachronistic). The page gives no founding year; 283 is Cliopatria's first shape.

region.text: the Saxon, Anglian and Jutish settlements in Britain

ledger.note: 449: Saxons cross to Britain. 'The traditional date for this invasion is 449 and is known as the Adventus Saxonum.' The settlers become part of Anglo-Saxon England (Cliopatria row from 441); the Saxons keep their homeland.

region.text: the land south of the Elbe-mouth core, Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia

ledger.note: 455: Old Saxony fills the land between the Elbe and the Rhine. 'As land became scarce, the Saxon population began to expand southward' (undated); the page gives 'the entire territory between the lower Elbe and Saale rivers almost to the Rhine' only for the later duchy. 455 is Cliopatria's jump; no opened page dates it.

region.text: the upper Weser, the Elbe and the North Sea coast

ledger.note: 555: Chlothar I attacks the Saxons. 'In 555, Chlothar attacked and conquered Saxons who had revolted in the upper valley of the Weser, Elbe, and the coast of the North Sea'; he demanded a large annual tribute.

region.text: Old Saxony

ledger.note: 556: the Saxons and Franks make peace. 'Between 555 and 556, the Saxons revolted again'; 'After a very bloody battle, the Saxons and Franks made peace'; he collected 'an annual tribute of 500 cows'. The Saxons page: Chlothar 'led an army in 556 to ravage Saxony and Thuringia'.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 772: Charlemagne invades Saxony. A Saxon raid burned the church at Deventer; he 'invaded, subjugated the Engrians, and destroyed the Irminsul' at Eresburg ('which the Franks destroyed in 772', Saxons page), 'reached the Weser' and took hostages.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 775: Charlemagne takes Saxony but for Nordalbingia. He took Sigiburg, beat the Engrians and the Eastphalians (whose leader Hessi converted) and left camps at Sigiburg and Eresburg: 'all Saxony except Nordalbingia was under his control', though the Saxons 'would not submit for long'. In 776 a rising destroyed Eresburg and Widukind fled to the Danes; Charlemagne restored control; in 777 the diet at Paderborn 'integrate[d] Saxony fully into the Frankish kingdom'.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 775: the first campaign ends in Frankish control of all but Nordalbingia.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 778: the Saxons rise while Charlemagne is in Spain. 'The next year, the Westphalians again invaded the Frankish Rhineland' (Widukind page); 'the Saxons advanced to Deutz on the Rhine and plundered along the river' (Saxons page). The year is the pages'; the full extent is Cliopatria's 778 shape.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 779: Charlemagne reconquers Saxony. 'In summer he conquered Eastphalia, Engria, and Westphalia'; at a diet near Lippspringe he 'divided the land into missionary districts and Frankish countships'. Nordalbingia is not named.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 782: Widukind's revolt. After Charlemagne appointed Saxon and Frankish counts, 'In the fall, Widukind led a revolt with attacks on churches'; he 'won the Battle of Süntel while Charles was campaigning against the Sorbs' and at the Massacre of Verden Charlemagne ordered 4,500 rebels beheaded (some historians dispute the number). The Widukind page: 'By 782, Widukind had returned from Denmark'; 'From 782 to 784, battles ... occurred annually'.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 782: the rebels hold the Saxon provinces. The revolt restores Saxon control in Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia until the winter campaigns of 783-785.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 785: Widukind submits. 'Widukind agreed to surrender in return for a guarantee that no bodily harm would be done to him' in the Bardengau and was baptised, possibly at Attigny, with Charlemagne as godfather (Widukind page); Charlemagne 'could have claimed to have conquered Saxony' and peace lasted about seven years (Saxon Wars page).

region.text: all Old Saxony, Nordalbingia included

ledger.note: 785: Saxony passes to the Franks. The Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae makes refusing baptism a capital offence; the Saxons hold no shape until the revolt of 793 (Cliopatria also has none for 788-792).

region.text: Old Saxony in revolt

ledger.note: 793: the Saxons rise again. The Westphalians rose in 792 against forced recruitment for the Avar wars; in 793 'Eastphalians and Nordalbingians joined the revolt'.

region.text: Old Saxony in revolt

ledger.note: 793: the rebels hold Old Saxony. The page names the three peoples that rose; the extent is Cliopatria's 793 shape.

region.text: Old Saxony

ledger.note: 794: the revolt is 'completely put down by 794'.

region.text: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia: Old Saxony without Nordalbingia

ledger.note: 794: Westphalia, Angria and Eastphalia pass to the Franks again; an Engrian rebellion in 796 was crushed 'quickly with Charlemagne's personal presence' and the death penalty for paganism was abolished in 797.

region.text: Nordalbingia, the Saxon land north of the Elbe (Holstein)

ledger.note: 798: the Obotrites beat the Nordalbingians at Bornhöved. 'The Obotrites under Prince Thrasco defeated the Saxons in the Battle of Bornhöved (798)'; the Saxon Wars page counts 2,800-4,000 Saxons killed, the Nordalbingia page 4,000 and 10,000 families deported.

region.text: Nordalbingia, the Saxon land north of the Elbe (Holstein)

ledger.note: 804: Charlemagne gives Holstein to the Obotrites. 'The part of their former land in Holstein north of Elbe was awarded to the Obotrites in 804, as a reward for their victory'; he deported 10,000 Nordalbingians to Neustria.

region.text: Nordalbingia, the Saxon land north of the Elbe (Holstein)

ledger.note: 804: the Saxon Wars end. 'In 804, the emperor Charlemagne conquered the Saxons' (Saxons page); Einhard: 'The war that had lasted so many years was at length ended by their acceding to the terms offered by the King', renouncing their religion and joining the Franks as one people. Old Saxony becomes the Carolingian Duchy of Saxony (804-1296); Nordalbingia goes to the Obotrites.

wars.name: Chlothar I's Saxon wars

zones.text: the upper Weser, the Elbe and the North Sea coast

wars.outcome: Chlothar conquered the revolted Saxons in 555, they revolted again, and after a bloody battle the two made peace on a tribute of 500 cows a year.
wars.note: The Saxons page: Chlothar 'led an army in 556 to ravage Saxony and Thuringia'; Chlothar's 531 Thuringian war needs no Saxon help (a later claim 'unsupported by contemporary sources').

wars.name: Frankish campaigns of Charles Martel against the Saxons
wars.outcome: No frontier moved: 718 he laid waste their country to the Weser, Lippe and Ruhr, 731 he defeated them, and in 738 he 'compelled the Saxons of Westphalia to submit and pay tribute'.
wars.note: The page also dates campaigns in the 720s without years.

wars.name: Frankish campaigns of Carloman and Pepin against the Saxons
wars.outcome: Carloman invaded Saxony in 743 and the brothers again in 744; Pepin marched in 748 and 753 and in 758 accepted a tribute of 330 horses a year; no frontier moved.

wars.name: Saxon Wars
wars.outcome: Charlemagne's thirty years of war: Eresburg and the Irminsul (772); Frankish control of all but Nordalbingia (775); the Saxon rising to Deutz (778); reconquest (779); Widukind's revolt, Süntel and Verden (782); Widukind's baptism (785); the revolt of 792-794; Bornhöved (798); the deportation of the Nordalbingians and the end in 804.
wars.note: The page's infobox lists 1,600 deported in 798 and 7,070 in 795; the Nordalbingia page puts 10,000 families after Bornhöved (798), the Saxon Wars text 10,000 in 804. The Widukind page dates Widukind's flight to Denmark in 777 where the Saxon Wars page has 776.

wars.name: Battle of Bornhöved (798)

zones.text: Nordalbingia, the Saxon land north of the Elbe (Holstein)

wars.outcome: Thrasco's Obotrites, allied with the Franks, defeated the Nordalbingian Saxons; the land north of the Elbe went to the Obotrites in 804.

certainty.note: The Saxon frontiers are rivers and forest (Ems, Weser, Elbe, Harz, Hesse) known only from Frankish campaigns and the later duchy; nothing is surveyed.

notes:
Cliopatria's Saxons row (283-799, 17 shapes) is: the Elbe-mouth core 283-454; Old Saxony 455-771; the Frankish campaign years 772-787 (a Westphalian patch lost 772-774; only Nordalbingia 775-777; all Old Saxony 778-787); no shape 788-792 (the Franks cover Saxony); all Old Saxony 793-799. Corrections: 772-774 stays whole (an incursion); 778 and 782-784 whole, 779-781 Nordalbingia only (the 779 reconquest of the three provinces), 785-792 none (Widukind's submission, 'conquered Saxony'), 793-794 whole, 795-804 Nordalbingia only. The dossier ends in 804 (Cliopatria's last Saxon shape is 799 and its Franks cover Saxony from 800). The Saxons are drawn as one state though the pages describe a league of four peoples (Westphalians, Angrians, Eastphalians, Nordalbingians) without a king; hence no capitals or rulers.
Open items: (1) the jump to Old Saxony in 455 is not on any opened page (the Chauci merger is dated to the 3rd century, the first Saxon reach to the Weser to 555); (2) the 5th-century Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain (449, Adventus Saxonum) is a split event only, the English side belongs to eu-11 (anglo-saxon-england row 441-533); (3) the Franks' dossier (eu-07) should carry the Saxon tribute (555-556, 738, 758) as vassal events if it uses them; (4) the ledger's contest/loss/gain pairs between 772 and 794 follow the Saxon Wars page's phases, Cliopatria's shapes agreeing only at 775-777 and 788-792; (5) the Saxons who went to Italy with the Lombards in 568 and 'returned to Gaul from Italy' in 572 (Saxons page) held no land. The gazetteer lacks Eresburg, Verden and the Saxon sub-regions (Engria/Angria, Eastphalia, Nordalbingia): the dossier uses Cliopatria's own shapes instead.
Budget: nine pages (Saxons, Old Saxony, Saxon Wars, Widukind, Nordalbingia, Chauci, Charles Martel, Chlothar I, Obotrites). Unverified: shapes 469-641 (boundary noise), 724. Pages disagree: Widukind's flight in 776 (Saxon Wars) or 777 (Widukind, Nordalbingia pages); the deportations 795 (infobox), 798 (Nordalbingia page) or 804 (Saxon Wars text); the Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae 785 (Saxon Wars) or 755-790 (Saxons page).
